chunks: From him, from Al-Hajjal, from Ubayd ibn Ishaq who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I am an owner of palm trees, so inform me of a limit to which I should adhere regarding it in terms of full measurement.' So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Intend full measurement. So if deficiency comes to you by hand, while you have intended full measurement, you are from the people of full measurement; and if you intend deficiency, then you give full measurement, you are from the people of deficiency.'

key_terms.الْوَفَاءُ: Full measurement or fulfillment of obligation
key_terms.صَاحِبُ نَخْلٍ: Owner of palm trees (referring to a merchant/producer)

ai.seo_question: How does intention affect the validity of commercial measurements in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that intention (niyyah) serves as the primary determinant of moral and legal status in commercial dealings, superseding mere physical accuracy. It illustrates that a merchant who intends to be fair but errs is rewarded for their sincerity, whereas one who intends to cheat but succeeds is still considered deficient in character. This underscores the spiritual dimension of trade in Shia tradition, where internal intent validates external actions.
